reviews.title: Misleading
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with this app and its misleading advertising. The app claims to recover deleted photos, leading customers to believe they can retrieve their original lost images. However, after getting through the paywall, you discover that the app actually uses AI to recreate photos rather than recover the originals. These are two completely different things, and that distinction should be made clear before customers are asked to pay.

Additionally, if you’re going to offer a free trial, advertise it upfront instead of burying it within the “Manage Subscription” tab. Customers should not have to dig through subscription settings to discover an option that should have been clearly presented from the beginning.

Beyond these misleading claims, this is essentially just another photo duplicate finder app. There is nothing particularly innovative or impressive about its functionality that justifies the way it is marketed.

Consumers deserve honest advertising, transparent pricing, and an accurate description of what they are purchasing. Unfortunately, this app falls short in all three areas.

I have requested a refund and would not recommend this app. The developers should prioritize transparency rather than creating unrealistic expectations to encourage purchases.

When I first installed the app it showed I had 763 things permanently deleted, I did the free 3 day trial and when that was installed. I had 0, no dealers photos no hidden stuff. reviews.title: Pointless
reviews.text: Honestly I tried this out. It’s not worth it. You can do everything it claims from your own photos or files. It literally just guides you through going to your recently deleted and hitting recover. Most of the time it even tells you to go to your own settings and do it yourself. And it displays pictures that are in your albums saying that oh this was hidden oh this is deleted, but it never was. It’s just a random photos that it uses to make you think you can get it when you already have it. And it wants to charge you $60 to do all of this.

reviews.title: Unreliable.
reviews.text: This is my first time typing a review and it's for good reason. Unfortunately this app cannot provide the services it claims to offer. I would also like to confirm that I only paid for the weekly subscription, not the yearly. If I'm charged $60, I will absolutely know. I bought the weekly subscription today, not the yearly. Reaffirming this statement so the developer knows. I will absolutely not be charged $60, I have already canceled my plan within the Apple Store as I had no ability to cancel the subscription within the app. It offered me two deals and during the last prompt it only allowed me to send an email to the support team for the app being too expensive or for technical issues. I sent an email anyway to confirm that I will not be charged $60 for an app that has proven unreliable. Whether or not this app can actually provide the services it offers, this app clearly has not proven useful whatsoever for myself. Again, if I'm charged $60 I will know. I read the previous reviews and many people came across this issue. I paid for less than $10 and that's it. Thank you.
